title: Zephyrine and the Verdict
premise: Zephyrine Sterling, archivist of Saint Verity's Cathedral, catalogues the effects of Elowen Marsh, a parishioner missing for three years and now declared legally dead — only to discover the woman's diary contains entries written after her disappearance, in ink that hasn't dried. Following the diary's clues into the cathedral's sealed crypt, Zephyrine learns Elowen faked her death to escape a conspiracy among the cathedral's benefactors, who laundered money through restoration funds and silenced anyone who noticed. The 'dead witness' everyone swears is gone is alive, hidden, and dying; Zephyrine must choose between protecting the institution that raised them and exposing the truth before Elowen's protectors bury them both. In the end, Zephyrine opens the crypt publicly, testifies at cost to their own freedom, and finds Elowen alive but changed — survival, they learn, was never free.
about_author: Juniper Dunmore is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing centuries of births, deaths, and quiet scandals in English cathedral archives. Their mysteries are known for ecclesiastical settings, unreliable paper trails, and protagonists who love institutions enough to break them.

chapters.title: The Inventory of the Missing
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Zephyrine's POV. Tasked with cataloguing Elowen Marsh's effects for the probate court, Zephyrine sorts a life into boxes: rosary, letters, a water-stained diary. The emotional beat is professional detachment beginning to crack as they realize they knew this woman's handwriting from the confession ledgers.

chapters.title: Ink That Hasn't Dried
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Reading the diary at night, Zephyrine reaches the date of Elowen's disappearance — and keeps reading. Entries continue for two more years, describing the crypt, the benefactors' meetings, fear. The beat is vertigo: the archive, their sanctuary, has just lied to them.

chapters.title: Three Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with flashbacks. They retrace the official record: police report, memorial service, the Dean's eulogy. Everyone remembers Elowen differently, and everyone insists she is dead. Zephyrine begins asking careful questions and notices how quickly the answers arrive, too smooth, too rehearsed.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The crypt beneath Saint Verity's has been sealed since a fire forty years ago; only the Dean and the head of the Restoration Trust hold keys. Zephyrine maps its layout from old plans and realizes the diary's descriptions match rooms no living person should know.

chapters.title: A Benefactor's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV shifts briefly to Sir Aldous Vane, chair of the Restoration Trust, then back to Zephyrine. Vane offers Zephyrine a generous promotion and a gentle warning about gossip. The beat is the first open menace wrapped in charity — the price of loyalty made explicit.

chapters.title: What the Confession Ledgers Say
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Cross-referencing decades of confessional records (anonymized, but patterned), Zephyrine finds a trail of parishioners who confessed financial anxieties, then vanished or died conveniently. The beat is dread compounding into certainty: Elowen was not the first.

chapters.title: The Diary Turns on Its Reader
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A later entry addresses the reader directly: 'If you are reading this, you are already inside it.' Pages describe Zephyrine's own habits — the late hours, the tea, the way they touch the stone arches. Someone wrote this expecting them. The beat is hunted intimacy.

chapters.title: Sister Bernadette Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: Zephyrine interviews the elderly sacristan who claims to have seen Elowen die by suicide — except her account contradicts itself across retellings, and a detail matches nothing in the coroner's file. The beat is compassion curdling: either Bernadette lies, or someone taught her what to remember.

chapters.title: Below the Fire Line
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Using a maintenance key copied from the 1980s plans, Zephyrine enters the crypt's outer corridor. They find fresh footprints in dust, a cot, tinned food — and a wall of newspaper clippings about the Trust. The beat is breathless confirmation: the witness lives here.

chapters.title: The Voice Behind the Wall
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A voice stops them before they go deeper: Elowen, gaunt and sharp, holding a crowbar. She doesn't trust the archivist; the diary was bait to see who came looking. The beat is a standoff between two people who both survived by being invisible.

chapters.title: Everything Elowen Saw
chapters.summary: Elowen's POV, told as her testimony over one night. She was the Trust's bookkeeper; she found the laundering, reported it, and was given a choice — disappear and live, or stay and die like the organist did in '89. The beat is grief for a self she had to kill to keep breathing.

chapters.title: The Price Already Paid
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Elowen reveals the cost of her survival: an innocent man, a groundskeeper, took the blame for discrepancies and died in prison. Her hiding isn't only cowardice — coming forward means his family learns the truth too. The beat is moral weight settling on both of them.

chapters.title: An Ally with a Key Ring
chapters.summary: Zephyrine recruits Sister Bernadette, showing her the contradictions gently until her real memory surfaces: she saw Elowen alive, and was paid to forget. The beat is fragile alliance — the first time truth has allies instead of witnesses.

chapters.title: Audit Season
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Using archival access, they quietly assemble the financial thread: shell restorations, double-billed stonework, payments routed through the Trust to offshore accounts. Vane's office begins requesting files. The beat is a race between paper and power.

chapters.title: They Search the Archive
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. While Zephyrine is lured to a fake meeting, Vane's men ransack the archive and take the diary. Zephyrine returns to shelves reordered by strangers' hands. The beat is violation — the institution has turned its own memory against its keeper.

chapters.title: The Decoy Diary
chapters.summary: Revealed in Zephyrine's POV: anticipating theft, Zephyrine had catalogued a forged diary in the real one's place; the stolen volume implicates a dead man, buying time. But Vane knows a forgery when he holds one. The beat is a gambit half-won, the clock now audible.

chapters.title: Bernadette Won't Answer
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Bernadette misses their rendezvous; her cell is empty, her prayer books arranged too neatly. Elowen wants to run; Zephyrine refuses to let another witness vanish. The beat is terror sharpening into resolve — running is how everyone lost so far.

chapters.title: Vespers for a Hostage
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A note in Bernadette's handwriting summons Zephyrine to the crypt after dark. It's a trap: Vane waits with the real diary and an offer — the archive, the promotion, silence — while below, Bernadette and Elowen are held. The beat is temptation at knife-point.

chapters.title: The Verdict of Stone
chapters.summary: Climax, Zephyrine's POV. During evening mass, Zephyrine triggers the fire alarm and the ancient crypt locks fail open before the congregation and arriving police. Vane's men scatter; Vane, cornered beneath four centuries of witnesses, tries to burn the ledger and is arrested in the smoke. The beat is catharsis through exposure.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, courtroom and aftermath. Elowen testifies, naming herself and the groundskeeper she couldn't save; Zephyrine testifies to the archive's role in the cover-up, implicating the Dean and risking their own prosecution for evidence handling. The beat is costly honesty — truth entered into the record at personal price.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Suspended pending inquiry, Zephyrine visits the groundskeeper's family and gives them his cleared name. Elowen, recovering, admits she no longer knows who she'd have been if she'd stayed. The beat is quiet reckoning: survival saved her body and cost everything else.

chapters.title: The Open Crypt
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Zephyrine's POV. Months later, the crypt reopens as a public memorial; Zephyrine, reinstated, catalogs its history honestly, including the ugly parts. Elowen visits, and the two stand where the diary began. The beat is earned peace — memory kept whole, loyalty finally aligned with truth.
